why:
All three checks were run and the finding's FACTS survive all three; it is refuted on the fourth ground the brief names -- it is an already-recorded, reasoned deviation, not a new defect. (1) Quote: verbatim at whats-new/2026-w23.md:96, inside the 'Other wins' grid, modulo Mintlify's markdown escaping and tags: 'OTEL\_RESOURCE\_ATTRIBUTES values are now attached as labels on metric datapoints, so you can slice usage metrics by custom dimensions like team or repo'. The whole
is that one sentence -- no second sentence reverses it. (2) Evidence: packages/shared/src/telemetry/usage-metrics.ts is real and says what was claimed. parseConfig (:332-:367) reads OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER (via otelExporterDisabled :318), OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_ENDPOINT, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TIMEOUT, OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_TEMPORALITY_PREFERENCE -- and nothing else. metricsPayload (:426-:427) hardcodes the resource to a single attribute, service.name='nessy-desktop'; datapoint attributes are the fixed four (backend, model, type, cost_reporting at :406-:411, and backend+model on cost at :419). Two small corrections to the claim's wording: the module does NOT read OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL (that name exists only in the managed-settings classification, managed-env.ts:167), and it DOES read the temporality preference, which the claim omits. (3) Consequence, checked separately from the identifier and in both directions. Up: no caller supplies resource attributes -- createUsageMetrics takes only an env record, and the managed-env classification (managed-env.ts:145-169) does not list OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES at all. Down: the sibling exporter is the same shape -- packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/otlp-telemetry.ts:309 also hardcodes resource attributes to service.name='nessy-desktop'. No renamed NESSY_ equivalent exists (grep of NESSY_[A-Z_]* over all src: only NESSY_ENABLE_TELEMETRY is telemetry-related; NESSY_RESOURCES* are app-bundle paths). grep -ran -a over packages/ and apps/ confirms zero source hits; the only hits in the tree are inside vendored third-party binaries (apps/electron/resources/bin/codex/*/codex-app-server and the bundled OTel JS SDK in packages/pi-agent-server/dist), i.e. runtimes whose own OTel SDK would honour the variable, never our metrics path. So the claimed state is factually accurate. WHY IT IS STILL REFUTED: this exact variable is named in a recorded deviation with a reason, so it is a decision, not a gap. docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-observability-and-cost.md:182 carries the category string 'documented, not implemented -- monitoring-usage.md:446 to :455 define the standard attribute set every metric shares: session.id, app.version, app.entrypoint, organization.id, user.account_uuid, user.account_id, user.id, user.email, terminal.type, and OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES passthrough, each with its own OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_* toggle. Ours carries none of them, and that is a decision rather than an omission: this is a bank fork ... A future operator who wants it should get the toggles, not a default', harvested into the generated register at 2026-07-29-deviation-register.md:210. I verified the row is the right one: monitoring-usage.md:455 is literally 'Keys from OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES | Custom attributes you set, such as department or team.id' with toggle OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES (default true), and :138 is the same toggle in the cardinality table -- the w23 'other win' is the release note for that row, not a new contract. The decision is also restated in shipped source at usage-metrics.ts:31-39: 'This fork exports NEITHER, nor any other row of that table: data points carry exactly backend, model, type, cost_reporting ... Any widening toward :442's table is a privacy decision to be made on purpose, not an omission to be patched.' It is additionally a duplicate of the residue already recorded in the sibling verdict data/phase2-verdicts/f069.json ('OTEL_SERVICE_NAME and OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES are not read; service.name is hardcoded nessy-desktop'). Not an inert-worklist section 3 row (I read all nine; none is telemetry). Honest caveat, so the refutation is not overstated: the recorded reason is a privacy argument that fits the identity rows (user.id, user.email, session.id) more squarely than the operator-set passthrough, which carries no user identity by default. If the owner wants slice-by-team, the work is re-deciding that recorded row and adding OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES parsing plus the OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES toggle -- a re-decision, not a bug fix.
correctedState: Accurate as a fact, wrong as a defect. Our OTLP metrics exporter (packages/shared/src/telemetry/usage-metrics.ts) does not read OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES: parseConfig (:332-:367) consumes only OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_ENDPOINT, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TIMEOUT, OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_TEMPORALITY_PREFERENCE (not _PROTOCOL, which the finding lists and which appears only in managed-env.ts:167's classification), and metricsPayload (:426-:427) hardcodes the resource to service.name='nessy-desktop' with datapoint attributes fixed at backend/model/type/cost_reporting. The sibling log exporter, packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/otlp-telemetry.ts:309, is identical. But this is a RECORDED DELIBERATE DEVIATION, not an unnoticed gap: the w23 line is the release note for monitoring-usage.md:455 ('Keys from OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES', toggle OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES, default true), a row of the :442-:455 standard-attribute table this fork declined wholesale, with the reason written in the plan (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-observability-and-cost.md:182), harvested into the generated register (2026-07-29-deviation-register.md:210) and restated in the shipped source header (usage-metrics.ts:31-39). It also duplicates the residue already logged in f069.json. Reopening it is a re-decision by the owner ('a future operator who wants it should get the toggles, not a default'), scoped as: parse the comma-separated key=value form with percent-decoding, add the OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES toggle, and attach the keys as datapoint labels in metricsPayload -- with the cardinality warning at monitoring-usage.md:346 as the reason the toggle exists.
